common_name: Imara XDR Red Impatiens (First Downy-Mildew-Resistant Seed-Grown Walleriana)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost; Imara XDR was bred by Syngenta Flowers as the first Impatiens walleriana seed series with a high degree of resistance to impatiens downy mildew, the disease that collapsed most seed-grown walleriana plantings after 2011.

directions: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost and transplant once nights stay reliably warm, into fertile, consistently moist, well-drained soil in partial shade to shade. Imara XDR Red carries the "XDR" (extreme downy mildew resistance) breeding that made this series the first seed-propagated Impatiens walleriana able to shrug off the pathogen that nearly eliminated seed-grown impatiens from the North American bedding-plant market. Flowers are a clear, saturated red held over a compact, well-branched mound that stays full and floriferous through humid summer stretches where older, susceptible strains thinned out and collapsed. Keep soil evenly moist, since impatiens wilt quickly once it dries out, and avoid overhead watering to further limit foliar disease pressure.

common_name: Imara XDR Orange Impatiens (First Downy-Mildew-Resistant Seed-Grown Walleriana)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost; Imara XDR was bred by Syngenta Flowers as the first Impatiens walleriana seed series with a high degree of resistance to impatiens downy mildew, the disease that collapsed most seed-grown walleriana plantings after 2011.

directions: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost and transplant once nights stay reliably warm, into fertile, consistently moist, well-drained soil in partial shade to shade. Imara XDR Orange shares the series' breakthrough resistance to impatiens downy mildew, letting gardeners grow economical seed-raised impatiens again in beds where the disease had wiped out traditional walleriana strains. Bright orange flowers cover a compact, uniform mound continuously from planting to frost without any deadheading needed. Water at the soil line rather than overhead and provide good airflow between plants to further discourage foliar disease.

common_name: Imara XDR White Impatiens (First Downy-Mildew-Resistant Seed-Grown Walleriana)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost; Imara XDR was bred by Syngenta Flowers as the first Impatiens walleriana seed series with a high degree of resistance to impatiens downy mildew, the disease that collapsed most seed-grown walleriana plantings after 2011.

directions: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost and transplant once nights stay reliably warm, into fertile, consistently moist, well-drained soil in partial shade to shade. Imara XDR White produces clean white flowers over glossy foliage on a compact, mounded plant, carrying the same breakthrough downy-mildew resistance that distinguishes the whole Imara XDR series from older seed-grown impatiens. Its pure flower color is especially useful for brightening deep shade and for pairing with the series' other saturated colors in mixed beds. Keep soil evenly moist at all times, since impatiens foliage wilts quickly once the root zone dries out.

common_name: Imara XDR Salmon Shades Impatiens (First Downy-Mildew-Resistant Seed-Grown Walleriana)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost; Imara XDR was bred by Syngenta Flowers as the first Impatiens walleriana seed series with a high degree of resistance to impatiens downy mildew, the disease that collapsed most seed-grown walleriana plantings after 2011.

directions: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost and transplant once nights stay reliably warm, into fertile, consistently moist, well-drained soil in partial shade to shade. Imara XDR Salmon Shades blends varying tones of warm salmon-pink across the planting rather than a single flat hue, giving subtle color variation while still carrying the series' breakthrough resistance to impatiens downy mildew. The compact, well-branched mounds stay full and continuously in bloom through humid summer weather that used to devastate susceptible seed-grown impatiens. Water consistently at the soil line and give plants good airflow to further limit foliar disease pressure.

common_name: Sonic White New Guinea Impatiens (Large-Flowered Vigorous Garden Impatiens)

planting.note: Set out vegetatively propagated transplants after all frost danger has passed into partial shade to partial sun in fertile, well-drained soil; Sonic is a Syngenta Flowers New Guinea impatiens series bred for notably large flowers and vigorous, robust garden performance.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in partial shade to partial sun, feeding regularly to sustain the large-scale flowering this series is known for. Sonic White bears clean white flowers that are noticeably larger than those of many other New Guinea impatiens, held over a sturdy, well-branched plant bred by Syngenta Flowers for vigorous, reliable landscape performance. As a New Guinea hybrid it tolerates considerably more sun and heat than traditional Impatiens walleriana and is naturally far less susceptible to impatiens downy mildew, the disease that devastated old-fashioned bedding impatiens. Keep soil evenly moist, especially during the hottest stretch of summer, since the large flowers and lush foliage draw more water than compact walleriana types.

common_name: Sonic Red New Guinea Impatiens (Large-Flowered Vigorous Garden Impatiens)

planting.note: Set out vegetatively propagated transplants after all frost danger has passed into partial shade to partial sun in fertile, well-drained soil; Sonic is a Syngenta Flowers New Guinea impatiens series bred for notably large flowers and vigorous, robust garden performance.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in partial shade to partial sun, and feed on a regular schedule to keep the sturdy plants blooming continuously. Sonic Red produces vivid, oversized red flowers on a vigorous, well-branched plant, part of a Syngenta Flowers New Guinea impatiens series noted for outperforming many older New Guinea types in garden trials. It tolerates more direct sun and heat than traditional Impatiens walleriana and carries the natural resistance to impatiens downy mildew typical of New Guinea hybrids. Water deeply and consistently through summer heat to keep the large flowers and glossy foliage from wilting.

common_name: Celebrette Red New Guinea Impatiens (Compact Mini New Guinea Impatiens)

planting.note: Set out vegetatively propagated transplants after all frost danger has passed into partial shade in fertile, well-drained soil; Celebrette is a Ball FloraPlant mini New Guinea impatiens series bred to stay notably smaller and more controlled than standard New Guinea impatiens, making it well suited to small pots and packs.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in partial shade to partial sun, feeding lightly through the season to support steady, well-branched growth. Celebrette Red is part of a Ball FloraPlant mini New Guinea impatiens series bred for a compact, mounded habit that stays proportioned to small containers and tight garden spaces rather than sprawling like standard-size New Guinea impatiens. It produces abundant, self-cleaning red flowers against glossy foliage from spring planting through frost, and like other New Guinea hybrids it is naturally far less prone to impatiens downy mildew than traditional Impatiens walleriana. Keep soil consistently moist, since the series' smaller pots and root systems dry out faster than full-size New Guinea impatiens.

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost; consistent moisture is essential, as impatiens wilt quickly in dry soil.

directions: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost. Beacon Lipstick is a later addition to PanAmerican Seed's AAS-recognized Beacon series, bred with strong resistance to impatiens downy mildew, the disease that collapsed most Impatiens walleriana bedding plantings in North America and Europe after 2011. Its hot pink, lipstick-toned flowers cover the classic mounded, flat-faced impatiens habit continuously from planting through frost, staying full in humid summer conditions where older, susceptible strains thinned out and died. Water at the soil line rather than overhead, and keep the soil consistently moist, since impatiens wilt rapidly once it dries out.

planting.note: Plant after all frost danger has passed; Impatiens walleriana is susceptible to impatiens downy mildew (IDM), which has devastated impatiens plantings across North America since 2011 — if IDM has been a problem in your area, consider New Guinea impatiens or SunPatiens instead. The Accent series performs best in well-drained conditions with good air circulation; do not overhead water.

directions: Plant in partial shade to shade in moist, well-drained, fertile, slightly acidic soil; Accent Salmon is part of the long-running Accent series of Impatiens walleriana, one of the industry benchmarks for seed-grown bedding impatiens before downy mildew reshaped the market. Its warm salmon-pink flowers cover a compact, mounded plant continuously from planting through frost without deadheading, and the dwarf, uniform habit of the Accent series made it a standard choice for mass bedding and flats for decades. Like other seed-grown Impatiens walleriana, it remains fully susceptible to impatiens downy mildew, so good air circulation and soil-level watering are important, and growers in areas with a known history of the disease should consider a resistant series such as Beacon or Imara XDR instead.
sources: All-America Selections — Impatiens Accent Series Awards
University of Florida IFAS Extension — Impatiens for Florida Landscapes
Louisiana State University AgCenter — Annual Flowers for Shade

common_name: Divine White New Guinea Impatiens (Seed-Grown Heat-Tolerant Impatiens)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 10-12 weeks before the last frost date, since Divine is a true seed-propagated New Guinea impatiens rather than a cutting-grown hybrid; transplant out after all danger of frost has passed into partial shade to partial sun.

directions: Sow seed indoors 10 to 12 weeks before the last frost date at a warm 70 to 80°F, since Divine is a seed-propagated New Guinea impatiens series bred as a more economical alternative to cutting-propagated lines like SunPatiens and Infinity. Divine White produces clean white flowers over a compact, well-branched mound, a bright option for lighting up shaded corners and evening gardens within the Divine color range. It tolerates considerably more sun than common Impatiens walleriana, performing best with some afternoon shade in hot climates, and carries good resistance to impatiens downy mildew. Keep the soil evenly moist and feed lightly through the season to sustain continuous bloom.

common_name: Divine Violet New Guinea Impatiens (Seed-Grown Heat-Tolerant Impatiens)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 10-12 weeks before the last frost date, since Divine is a true seed-propagated New Guinea impatiens rather than a cutting-grown hybrid; transplant out after all danger of frost has passed into partial shade to partial sun.

directions: Sow seed indoors 10 to 12 weeks before the last frost date at a warm 70 to 80°F, since Divine is a seed-propagated New Guinea impatiens series bred as a more economical, easy-to-germinate alternative to vegetatively propagated New Guinea impatiens. Divine Violet carries rich violet-purple flowers over a compact, well-branched mound, a cool-toned complement to the brighter reds and oranges elsewhere in the Divine series. It tolerates considerably more sun than common Impatiens walleriana while still performing best with some afternoon shade in hot climates, and carries good resistance to impatiens downy mildew. Keep soil consistently moist and provide light regular feeding to sustain continuous bloom from spring through frost.

common_name: SunPatiens Spreading White Impatiens (Mounding Sun-Tolerant New Guinea Impatiens)

planting.note: Set out transplants after all frost danger has passed into full sun to partial shade in fertile, well-drained soil; SunPatiens Spreading is the mid-size, mounding tier of the SunPatiens line, with finer-textured foliage and an earlier trailing habit than the other tiers.

directions: Plant in full sun to partial shade in fertile, well-drained soil, feeding regularly to support the broad, mounding growth this tier of the SunPatiens line is bred for. SunPatiens Spreading White forms a wide, trailing mound covered in clean white flowers from spring through frost, with a finer leaf texture and earlier trailing habit than the other SunPatiens Spreading colors. Like the rest of the SunPatiens breeding line, it carries strong resistance to impatiens downy mildew and tolerates considerably more sun and heat than traditional shade impatiens. Its spreading habit makes it well suited to large hanging baskets, window boxes, and ground-level mass plantings where a trailing white accent is wanted.

common_name: SunPatiens Spreading Red Impatiens (Mounding Sun-Tolerant New Guinea Impatiens)

planting.note: Set out transplants after all frost danger has passed into full sun to partial shade in fertile, well-drained soil; SunPatiens Spreading is the mid-size, mounding tier of the SunPatiens line, sized between the tidy Compact series and the tall, upright Vigorous series.

directions: Plant in full sun to partial shade in fertile, well-drained soil, feeding regularly to support the broad, mounding growth this tier of the SunPatiens line is bred for. SunPatiens Spreading Red forms a wide, quick-spreading mound covered in bright, clear scarlet-red flowers from spring through frost, filling more horizontal space than the upright Vigorous series while growing fuller than the Compact series. Like the rest of the SunPatiens line, it carries strong resistance to impatiens downy mildew and tolerates considerably more sun and heat than traditional shade impatiens. Its broad, fast-filling habit makes it well suited to large hanging baskets, ground-level mass plantings, and filling wide garden beds without staking.

planting.note: Set out transplants after the last frost into partial shade to partial sun in fertile, well-drained soil; Bounce Cherry is a downy-mildew-resistant impatiens hybrid bred to replace traditional Impatiens walleriana in beds where the disease has been a problem.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in partial shade to partial sun, and feed and water regularly to keep the vigorous, well-branched mounds blooming without interruption. Bounce Cherry is a vegetatively propagated interspecific impatiens hybrid bred with resistance to impatiens downy mildew, covering its mounded habit in bright cherry-red flowers from spring through frost. Like other Bounce colors, it rebounds quickly after a rain or an accidental broken stem, springing back into full, tidy bloom within days. Give it more consistent moisture than SunPatiens types, since Bounce is bred primarily for shade and part-sun performance rather than full-sun heat tolerance, and pinch leggy stems in midsummer to keep plantings dense.
sources: Selecta One — Bounce Impatiens series notes
University of Florida IFAS Extension — Bedding Plant Trials

common_name: Peppermint Stick Balsam (Victorian Heirloom Candy-Striped Garden Balsam)

planting.note: Direct sow seeds shallowly on the soil surface (they need light to germinate) after the last frost in well-drained, fertile, slightly acidic to neutral soil in partial shade; Peppermint Stick is a rediscovered Victorian-era heirloom balsam, once a fixture of 19th-century cottage gardens, with spotted and striped flowers.

directions: Direct sow seeds shallowly after the last frost into well-drained, fertile, slightly acidic to neutral soil in partial shade, or start indoors a few weeks earlier for an earlier bloom. Peppermint Stick is a rediscovered heirloom double-flowered garden balsam dating to the Victorian era, bearing ruffled, camellia-like flowers candy-striped and spotted in bright white and candy-apple red along an upright stem, rather than held above the foliage as in modern bedding impatiens. Like other Impatiens balsamina selections it is notably more heat- and sun-tolerant than Impatiens walleriana, taking partial shade comfortably and tolerating brief stretches of fuller sun where soil stays moist. The explosive seed pods fling seed when touched, true to the genus name, and plants often self-sow in favorable gardens for a volunteer crop the following year.
